description: Change of use of an existing detached outbuilding to habitable space to be used as a granny annex
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015, no window or other opening (other than those shown on the submitted and approved plan,) shall be formed in the flank wall(s) of the building(s) hereby permitted, unless specific permission under the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 has first been sought and obtained in writing from the Local Planning Authority.
In order to ensure a satisfactory development that will not result in any loss of privacy or damage to the environment of neighbouring properties which exist or may be proposed in the future.
The garden area shall not be subdivided at any time and nor shall there be any additional pedestrian or vehicular accesses into the site.
In order that the annex approved remains ancillary to the main dwelling.

Any residential occupation of the building hereby approved shall be limited to immediate family members of the family occupying the main dwelling at 22 Ravenswood Close, Romford for residential purposes and shall not be occupied by any other persons.
In order that the annex approved remains ancillary to the main dwelling.
The outbuilding hereby permitted shall not be arranged or disposed of as a separate unit of residential accommodation from the use of the main dwelling. In particular it shall not be rented out.
In order that the annex approved remains ancillary to the main dwelling.

Statement Required by Article 35(2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management) Order 2015: No significant problems were identified during the consideration of the application, and therefore it has been determined in accordance with paragraph 39 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

You are informed that this decision has been approved on the basis that the outbuilding is in use by a member of the family. If the premises were failed to be used for the intended purpose as declared in the submitted statement, then this permission would be invalid, and in breach of condition, with the council likely to initiate proceeding to remedy the breach which may include prosecution.
